questions.question: What is the amortized time complexity of `list.append()` in CPython?

options.text: O(1) because CPython overallocates memory geometrically
O(n) because it always copies all elements
O(log n) due to binary tree allocation

questions.explanation: CPython uses an over-allocation growth factor (`new_allocated = size + (size >> 3) + ...`), making appends O(1) amortized across n operations.

questions.question: Why is `queue.pop(0)` inefficient when implemented with a standard Python list?

options.text: It requires shifting all remaining n-1 pointers to the left in contiguous memory (O(n))
It frees the entire underlying array
It invokes garbage collection on every call
It converts the list to a tuple internally

questions.explanation: Because `PyListObject` maintains a contiguous array of pointers, deleting the first element requires moving all subsequent pointers one position left using memmove.
